subject: af-con
title: AF.CON.------RE.ST.
description: Diagram in WAC-27, the third on book p229. (C)AF-CON (affinity convergence) is crossed with RE-ST (restructuralism). Embedded in the Euro-American discussion: when affinity-convergence (the bringing-together of disparate affinity tendencies under one project) is crossed with restructuralism, what's the resulting structural shape? Two upstream feeds: AFL-DT (affinity dictates) → INFO-OR (information order), and LANG-DY (language dynamics) → INFO-OR; LANG-DY also branches to POST (postulation). INFO-OR is the central hub, fanning to LG-EXT (logical extension), RE-ST (the crossing partner), and AF-CON (the subject). A separate sub-chain runs PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) → SOC-RT (social reality) → INTR (interpretation), and PROG-CONT → INFO-DOC (information documentation). IF-ST-DY (infra-structure dynamics) feeds AF-CON. Structural argument: affinity convergence is produced by information order, which is itself produced by the convergence of affinity dictates and language dynamics — meaning the affinity-coalescence Braxton is describing requires both the inherited affinity-tendency-dictates and the language-dynamics layer to organize them. Restructuralism is a sibling output of information order, not downstream of affinity-convergence — they are co-produced. The progressional-continuance sub-chain runs separately, producing the interpretation/documentation outcomes that register the convergence in the historical record.
